ここまで３勝３分６敗の長崎は、勝点12で14位。１勝５分６敗の東京Ｖは、勝点８で18位。安定した成績を残せていない両チームにとって、今節は勝点の近い相手と戦う試合であり、是が非でも勝点３が欲しい一戦となる。 長崎は前々節、首位を争う広島に４－０で勝利。相手に退場者が出たとはいえ、それまでにも２点を挙げており、紛れもない快勝劇だった。 ところが、前節は浦和に０－１で敗戦。高木 琢也監督が試合後、「攻撃に出たときのかみ合わせやつながっていく部分が、いつもよりもちょっと遅い。マインドのほうも遅くなってしまい、全体が活性化できないところが多くあった」と振り返ったように、連戦の影響かチーム全体の体の重さが否めず、特に後半は相手にボールを握られる時間が続いた。 なかなか流れに乗り切れない時期が続くが、今節はホームでの試合となる。今季の長崎はアウェイの６戦で勝点１にとどまる一方、ホーム６戦では３勝２分１敗で勝点11。ピッチとスタンドが極めて近く、満員のサポーターの後押しを得られることの効果は、結果が表している。勝点３が欲しい今節も、ホームの利を生かして勝利を目指す。 前節で連戦が終わり、十分なコンディションで挑める今節。長崎の攻撃のクオリティーにおいて重要な役割を担う マテウス ジェズス にかかる期待は大きい。浦和戦ではやや疲労を感じさせたが、万全な状態であれば圧倒的な個の力を発揮できる。前線に起点を作れるだけでなく、左足の一振りで試合の流れを一変させられる背番号10のプレーに注目だ。 マテウス・ジェズスには“一振り”で試合を決められる個の力がある（写真は2026/27 Ｊ１第11節・広島戦） 東京Ｖは前節、同じく残留を争う福岡に３－１で勝利。最後まで勝利への執念を感じさせ、待望の今季初勝利を挙げた。前々節・横浜FM戦では０－２から追いついて勝点１をつかんでおり、着実にチーム状態は上向いている。 特に攻撃面の改善は顕著で、高い位置までボールを運んだ際には次々と後ろの選手が追い越していく。攻撃で重要な役割を担うのが、福岡戦で先制点を挙げた 熊取谷 一星 だ。豊富な運動量と動き出しの質によって、チーム全体の攻撃に変化を加えられる。今節は 染野 唯月 が出場停止から復帰するが、いずれにせよ現在の東京Ｖにおいて熊取谷 一星は外せない存在ではないか。 また、直近３試合で途中出場が続く 森田 晃樹 にかかる期待も大きい。相馬 直樹監督は前節の試合後、「今回も途中から森田に入ってもらいましたけど、森田のところから攻撃の時間を作れるようになったんじゃないか」と評価しており、明治安田Ｊ１第４節・鹿島戦以来のスタメン出場もそろそろ期待できそうだ。 途中出場が続く森田晃樹。今節の起用法は？ ２試合ぶりの勝利を目指す長崎か、前節の勢いそのままに連勝を目指す東京Ｖか。浮上を狙う両チームによる、楽しみな一戦が幕を開ける。 ［ 文：椎葉 洋平 ］

明治安田Ｊ１第13節で顔を合わせる町田とＧ大阪は、異なるアジアのコンペティションを戦っている者同士。ホームの町田は前年度大会をＧ大阪が制したAFCチャンピオンズリーグTwo（ACL Two）を戦っている真っ最中で、今節の３日前にアウェイでのグループＧ第３節・上海申花（中国）戦を終えたばかりだ。 「（ACL Twoで）Ｇ大阪に続く日本勢連覇を目指している」（ 昌子 源 ）町田は、上海申花戦から中２日でＧ大阪戦に臨むが、Ｊ１制覇を明確な目標に掲げている以上、過密日程は宿命。ましてや上海申花戦はリーグ戦で出場機会の少ない選手たちを中心に戦っているため、上海からの移動による負担は大きいにしても、リーグ戦の主力メンバーは決して過密日程をエクスキューズにはできないはずだ。 なお、町田は公式戦が立て込んでいた10月の全７試合をいずれもクリーンシートで終える“離れ業”をやってのけた。その要因は、卓越したセービング能力でゴールにカギをかけている守護神・ 谷 晃生 を抜きにして語ることはできない。 たとえ相手のアタッカー陣が屈強な３バックの守備網を突破したとしても、“最後の砦”として谷 晃生が立ちはだかっていることに恐れおののく対戦相手も少なくない。リーグ前節、谷 晃生との１対１を止められてしまった神戸の ジェアン パトリッキ は「相手のGKが一枚上手だった」と舌を巻いた。いまの町田を相手にゴールをこじ開けるのは、決して容易なことではないということだ。 また近年の谷 晃生は、チームが地上戦でボールを動かしながらアタッキングエリアへと進入していく過程に関与することも増えてきた。これまではロングキックで数多くのチャンスを演出してきたため、谷 晃生のイメージとしては、“ドカ蹴り”の印象も強いが、「練習の賜物」と技術を高めてきた町田の守護神は、相手のポジション取りを逆手にとった“後出しじゃんけん”に匹敵する配球を決して苦にはしていない。Ｇ大阪とはＪ１百年構想リーグで対戦がなかったため、アカデミー出身GKの進化に驚くサポーターは多いかもしれない。 鉄壁の守備を支える谷晃生。配球面でも技術の高さが光っている 一方でアウェイに乗り込むＧ大阪は、町田戦の４日前にAFCチャンピオンズリーグElite 2026/27リーグステージ第３節のブリーラム・ユナイテッド（タイ）戦をホームで戦った。大阪からの移動があるとはいえ、町田と比較して、今節までの試合間隔は１日長く、上海遠征明けの町田よりはコンディションが整っていると言えるだろう。 公式戦７試合連続で無失点を記録している町田の堅守をいかに攻略するか。そのキーマンとして挙げられる選手の筆頭格は、ブリーラム・ユナイテッド戦でも難易度の高いシュートを決めた 宇佐美 貴史 だろう。宇佐美 貴史は2024年のＪ１開幕節で谷 晃生が守るゴールマウスに直接FKを叩き込んだアタッカー。目下公式戦３試合連続ゴール中で元チームメートのクセを熟知している“Ｇ大阪の至宝”が、町田撃破のカギを握る。 堅守の町田に対し、Ｇ大阪は公式戦３戦連発中の宇佐美貴史がキーマンだ ［ 文：郡司 聡 ］

Click HERE to watch his full pre-match media conference. The hosts will be looking to get on the board for the season having suffered consecutive 2-1 defeats to Macarthur FC and Brisbane Roar respectively in the opening two rounds. And Griffiths believes that a front foot approach is they key to getting the better of an Adelaide side who lost 2-1 to Sydney FC in their only ALM outing so far this term. “We have to be very focused and make sure we do our jobs,” he said, “but we’re also at home and we want to take the game to Adelaide and put on a very, very good performance in front of our own fans. “I think the boys are really looking forward to performing in front of our Members and fans. “It’s been a while and we’re excited about it.” The Head Coach went on to stress that while the points return from the opening two rounds was disappointing, there were plus points to be found in each of the games. “What we need to focus on, especially with this young group, is the performance,” he said. “I thought in the first game against Macarthur, the performance was good but we didn’t get the points and then it was 50% in terms of performance in the Brisbane game. “So what the boys have been focusing on is being ready for this game and making sure we’re sticking to our processes. “We look at all the positives and the things they’re doing well and get at the game that way. “That’s the key message this week.” Adelaide will be a familiar opponent for Glory after the sides met twice in last month’s pre-season Regional Roadie and Griffiths is keenly aware of the threat Airton Andrioli’s men will pose. “Adelaide will provide different problems [to Macarthur and Brisbane],” he said. “They’re a very good team, a very dangerous team and they change [formations] a lot. “Against Sydney, I felt that they had some success playing through, but probably lacked a bit of final product. “But they had their chances to hurt them.” In terms of squad news, meanwhile, Griffiths reported that Trent Ostler (hamstring) and Brian Kaltak (knee) are on track to return to training next week, joining Charbel Shamoon who is closing in on a making a full recovery from his foot injury. He also confirmed that Jaiden Kucharski and Will Freney are in contention to start on Sunday afternoon, with Giovanni De Abreu another putting his hand up for selection. “It’ll be great to potentially have JK back in the starting team,” he said “The whole group is fitter than what it was in the previous two weeks and we have quality players coming back into the squad who’ve had another week in training. “That’s a real positive; the strength of the squad is slowly getting there. “JK and Gio are both training really well now and putting in good training performances, so we’re expecting to see them out there on Sunday. “Will was great against Macarthur and we really missed him in the game against Brisbane. “He’s one of those players that people don’t notice, but he has a huge effect on the team. “We’re really excited to have him back and with Gio looking to get more minutes as well, our midfield is starting to strengthen.” As for Adelaide, they followed their defeat at the hands of Sydney FC by losing 2-0 to Singaporean side Lions City Sailors in the AFC Champions League Two on Thursday evening. Highly-rated young striker Brody Burkitt scored their goal against the Sky Blues and he is likely to start against Glory, as are experienced duo Craig Goodwin and Ryan Kitto, plus Dutch import Joshua Smits who is widely regarded as one of the best goalkeepers in the competition. Smits’ compatriot Bart Vriends, however, remains sidelined by injury, as does Dylan Pierias who has scored four times in his 15 appearances against Glory. Sunday will mark the 60th overall meeting between the two sides and the 30th in WA, of which Glory have won 11 to the Reds’ nine. This fixture has provided plenty of excitement in recent years, with the last 10 clashes yielding a combined aggregate of 41 goals. Click HERE for full match highlights. Click HERE for Adam Griffiths’ post-match media conference. The New Zealander capitalised upon an under-hit back-pass from Joel King on the hour-mark, finding the net with his first touch after being introduced from the bench only seconds earlier. But by that time Glory were trailing to first-half goals from Justic Vidic and Tae-hee Nam and were ultimately unable to find an equaliser during a frantic finale in the Queensland capital. After a competitive if largely uneventful opening quarter, the hosts began to build up a head of steam and eventually made the breakthrough just short of the half-hour mark. Seizing upon a defensive error, Tate Russell made inroads down the right before slipping a low cross into the path of Vidic who calmly tapped home from close range. Glory almost responded immediately, Pieter Jacobsz firing into the side-netting after excellent approach work from Sam Sutton, but Roar remained in the ascendancy and doubled their lead shortly before the break. When Glory were only able to half-clear their lines, the ball fell for Nam and he arrowed a spectacular volley into the top corner from the edge of the box. A response was required from the visitors at the start of the second half and they very nearly produced it inside the opening two minutes as substitute Jaiden Kucharski linked up with Tom Lawrence in the box, but after cleverly beating a couple of defenders, the skipper was just unable to squeeze his shot inside the far post. Vidic then went close to taking the hosts out of sight when his low shot clipped the outside of the post only for Glory to make the most of that let-off by pulling one back moments later. There looked to be little danger when King attempted to roll the ball back to George Plusnin in the home goal, but he did not get enough on the pass and the alert Ellis raced in to send a toe-poke finish into the bottom corner. With the tide seemingly turning in their favour, Glory poured forward in search of a late leveller and created a golden opportunity in the 75th minute. Jaiden Kucharski, who made a lively cameo off the bench, played Stefan Colakovski in behind with a perfectly-timed through-ball, but he was unable to find the target in a one-on-one situation. That was as close as Glory came to securing a first point of the season, with the game becoming increasingly fractious in the final minutes. New signing Jay O’Shea was introduced from the bench against his former club with ten minutes left and showed some nice touches, but Roar held on to consign Glory to a second consecutive 2-1 defeat on the road. Click HERE for full match highlights. Click HERE for Adam Griffiths’ post-match media conference. Adam Griffiths’ side had looked on course to secure victory in Round One for the first time since 2014 when Tom Lawrence fired them in front shortly before the hour-mark. But the Bulls levelled things up via a hotly-disputed, re-taken Ryan Fraser penalty four minutes from time and then snatched all three points moments later courtesy of a header from former Glory man Jonathan Aspropotamitis. There was little sign of the drama to come during a largely disjointed first half in which neither side seriously threatened to break the deadlock. Ben Gibson shot narrowly wide early on and Luke Vickery did likewise on the half-hour mark, while Sebastian Despotovski missed Glory’s best chance, but neither goalkeeper was called into action across the opening stanza. The second half, however, provided far more in the way of action, beginning with Lawrence’s superb opening goal. A pocket of space some 30m out from goal was all the Welshman required and he strode towards the edge of the box before slotting into the bottom corner with pinpoint accuracy. Pieter Jacobsz then almost marked his Glory debut in style, firing narrowly wide having been picked out by fellow-substitute Sam Sutton and at that stage a hard-earned away victory appeared to be within touching distance. The complexion of the game changed entirely in the 80th minute, however, with referee Shaun Evans and the VAR very much to the fore. Glory midfielder Calem Nieuwenhof was penalised for handball in the box, even though he appeared to have been impeded by Bernardo Oliviera as he attempted to challenge Tatsuki Nara. VAR nonetheless upheld the penalty decision, Ryan Fraser stepped up to take it and Matt Sutton pulled off a stunning, one-handed save to block the Scottish import’s spot-kick. But Glory’s reprieve proved to be short-lived as VAR penalised Cher Deng for encroaching into the box, ordering a re-take which Fraser managed to convert despite Sutton again guessing right. This time several players from both teams appeared to encroach into the box and yet bafflingly, no action was taken by the match officials. The Glory players and staff were left seething and to rub salt into the wound, the Bulls promptly grabbed what proved to be the winner in the 89th minute. Fraser was the architect this time, curling in a free-kick from the right which was nodded home by Aspropotamitis. That left precious little time for Glory to muster a response and they were unable to do so as the home side held on claim all three points. We’ve got lots of games and lots of travelling, but I’d rather be in this situation than not having to play those games. “It’s obviously a challenge for us as a club and as a team, but there’s no better way of improving and getting stronger, and also helping to develop those players playing in those conditions. “That’s where we want to be. We just have to stay focused. It’s still early in the A-League season and we’re in a good position in Asia, so we just have to keep going.” On the importance of the collective… “I always try to emphasise the fact that football is a collective game. It’s good to have those individual players with quality and experience in the squad, but for me, it’s more about what we do as a collective. “You have to be very strong as a unit, working together. We’ve got important players in the squad, but we all have to perform to the best of our capabilities, and that’s what makes the team stronger. “We have to put behind us what happened in those last two matches and bounce back on Sunday. Hugo Gomes then broke the deadlock for the visitors, and Lennart Thy added a second deep into stoppage time. It was a disappointing way to finish, but it did not reflect the control the Reds showed for much of the match, and there are positives to take from the performance. Full time: Adelaide United 0-2 Lion City Sailors at Hindmarsh Stadium. United had 58.4% of possession against the Sailors at Hindmarsh Stadium Joshua Smits made five saves to keep the Reds level deep into the second half Lion City Sailors scored in the 80th minute and again deep into stoppage time Airton Andrioli made attacking changes as United pushed for a breakthrough First half Adelaide United lined up in a 4-2-3-1 at Hindmarsh Stadium, with Brody Burkitt leading the line and Craig Goodwin, Juan Muñiz and Amlani Tatu working behind him. Lion City Sailors set up in a 5-4-1 and were the sharper side early, with Joshua Smits called on to turn aside Kyoga Nakamura’s left-footed effort from outside the box in the seventh minute. The visitors kept coming. Antonio Mance and Matthias Phaëton both sent efforts just wide of the right post in the 11th and 12th minutes, and Smits then saved Phaëton’s shot from the centre of the box in the 15th. The Sailors were forced into an early change in the 23rd minute, Ilhan bin Fandi Ahmad replacing the injured Mance. Smits denied Nakamura again from the right side of the box, before Hugo Gomes hit the bar with a header from a Giovanni Haag corner delivery in the 25th minute. Tatu offered a first reply for the Reds two minutes later, a right-footed effort from outside the box that drifted left. The pressure did not let up. Smits saved from Phaëton in the 30th minute and from Nakamura in the 35th, and Ilhan bin Fandi Ahmad also headed against the woodwork from another Haag corner in the 33rd. The Reds held firm through a testing spell. United finished the half on the front foot. Burkitt’s shot from the right side of the box was saved by Victor Aznar after Goodwin’s pass in the 42nd minute, and Tatu had two more sights of goal on the break, both missing to the left. Anselmo de Moraes was booked for a foul in between, and the sides went in level at 0-0 after two minutes of added time. Second half Jay Barnett came on at the break for Anselmo de Moraes, and United began the second half on the front foot. Ryan Kitto sent a header over the bar from a Juan Muñiz corner delivery, and Panagiotis Kikianis then headed wide from another Muñiz corner as the Reds looked for an early breakthrough. Lion City Sailors found their feet again around the 55-minute mark, with Bart Ramselaar and Ilhan bin Fandi Ahmad both shooting off target in quick succession. Andrioli responded by refreshing his attack just before the hour, Joey Garuccio replacing Muñiz and Jonny Yull replacing Goodwin, while the Sailors swapped Jorge Karse for Ryhan Euan Griffin Stewart. Diogo Costa and Phaëton both fired over on the counter either side of a blocked Harry Crawford effort, and Ajak Riak replaced Tatu on 70 minutes as United kept pressing. Garuccio tested Victor Aznar from distance, then Burkitt headed a Yull cross wide and forced a save with a right-footed effort from outside the box, with Sotirios Phillis booked for a foul along the way. The deadlock broke in the 80th minute. Lennart Thy had been introduced three minutes earlier, and from a corner Hugo Gomes saw a header blocked before finishing left-footed from very close range into the centre of the goal. Smits had kept United level until then. Ben Folami replaced Crawford as the Reds pushed for an equaliser. Kitto fired high and wide, Riak was denied by Aznar, and Folami, Ethan Alagich, Kikianis and Kitto all had efforts blocked or missed across four added minutes. Then Phaëton released Thy on a fast break and he finished left-footed into the centre of the goal to make it 0-2. Full time It is a frustrating end to a night the Reds were in for so long, and the timing of the two goals makes it sting. The Sailors carried more threat on the night, with 25 shots and eight on target against United’s 16 and five, and they took their chances when it mattered, leaving United with nothing from a match in which they had plenty of the ball. Sydney responded after the interval with two goals in the space of nine minutes, and United were left searching for a leveller they could not quite find. It was a result that did not reflect the control the Reds showed in the first half, and there are positives to take from the performance. Full time: Sydney FC 2-1 Adelaide United at Allianz Stadium Brody Burkitt gave the Reds the lead in the 16th minute, and United went in at half-time ahead Rhys Youlley (64′) and Oriola Sunday (73′) scored Sydney’s goals in the space of nine minutes after the hour to turn the match United had 52.3% of possession and made a triple change at 76 minutes in search of an equaliser First half Adelaide United had its first real sight of goal at Allianz Stadium in the 14th minute, when Anselmo de Moraes sent a right-footed effort from outside the box high and wide after Craig Goodwin’s pass. It was an early sign of the confidence the Reds were playing with. Two minutes later, United had the lead. Brody Burkitt took the chance on himself, firing a right-footed shot from the centre of the box into the middle of the goal to put the Reds 1-0 up. Burkitt was booked a minute later for excessive celebration, and Sydney pushed back. Joshua Smits did well to save Alexandar Popović’s shot from the centre of the box, and Al Hassan Touré went close with a right-footed effort from the right side of the box that just missed the top right corner. United kept their composure and held a share of the ball. Juan Muñiz had a left-footed attempt from outside the box blocked on the half-hour, and after Takahiro Sekine was cautioned for a foul, another Muñiz strike from distance was also blocked. Ben Garuccio was shown a yellow card in first-half stoppage time, and Ryan Kitto drilled a left-footed shot from the centre of the box just wide from Muñiz’s set-piece cross right before the whistle. The Reds took a 1-0 lead into the break. Second half United started the second half on the front foot, with Anselmo forcing a save from Harrison Devenish-Meares from outside the box straight after the restart, set up by Goodwin. Sydney FC had their first sights of goal soon after, and Wataru Kamijo was booked in the 51st minute for a foul as the hosts began to push higher. The Reds kept probing, with Kitto heading wide from a Muñiz cross after a corner. Smits then made a good save to deny Touré from the right side of the box, before Muñiz saw an effort blocked from a tight angle on the left. Sydney made the first change when Joe Lacey replaced Kamijo, and Jonny Yull came on for Kitto a minute later. Then, in the 64th minute, Rhys Youlley levelled with a right-footed strike from outside the box into the bottom left corner, set up by Tiago Quintal, who was replaced by Akol Akon a minute later. Burkitt tested Devenish-Meares from distance in the 72nd minute, but Sydney struck again a minute later. Oriola Sunday finished from the left side of the six-yard box, with Touré providing the assist, to put the hosts 2-1 ahead. Airton Andrioli responded with a triple change in the 76th minute, bringing on Ajak Riak, Feyzo Kasumovic and Joey Garuccio for Burkitt, Sotirios Phillis and Muñiz, and Smits denied Sunday a minute later. Amlani Tatu replaced Goodwin in the 84th, and the Reds pressed deep into stoppage time through Riak, Anselmo and Ethan Alagich, but Sydney held on. Feyzo Kasumovic of Adelaide United looks dejected after the match at Allianz Stadium. (Photo: Jason McCawley/Getty Images) Full time It was a disappointing way to finish an afternoon that had started so well for Adelaide United, with the Reds unable to hold on to a half-time lead and going down 2-1 to Sydney FC at Allianz Stadium. Burkitt’s goal gave United a deserved advantage, and the numbers show the Reds were competitive throughout: 52.3% of possession, 484 passes to Sydney’s 437 with 397 of them accurate, reflecting the intent to play through the hosts. Smits made three saves to keep the Reds in the contest, and there was plenty in the way United controlled the opening stages that supporters can take encouragement from. Following victory in Thailand, Andrioli believes United is ready for the different demands of domestic competition, with collective strength and trust in the players at the heart of his approach. Speaking ahead of the Sydney clash, Andrioli discussed building on last season, opportunities within the squad and the importance of delivering United’s game plan. On the challenge posed by Sydney… “They’re a good side. Obviously, they’ve got good players. Sydney always have a strong team. “But for us, it’s more focusing on what we do as a team and building on the belief and the confidence that we always try to instil into our players. “Stick to our plan, stick to what we do best, and play to get a result.” On collective strength… “For me, it’s more about building that collective unity amongst the players. Everybody understands that football is a collective game. “We don’t rely necessarily on individuals, but if the collective is good and strong, then individuals can flourish. “We just want to have a strong, cohesive squad that plays together as a team and maximise that, and then let the individuals flourish as they come through.” On taking the next step… “We’re extremely happy with what we achieved last year, but we need to put that behind us. “To maintain that or go to another level is another thing. We know the challenge ahead of us. The A-League is very competitive. “Whatever was done last year, we have to learn from it, get better and stronger in order to repeat that and maybe go one step further.” On opportunities within the squad… “I have plenty of confidence in the players we have in the squad. We have players that can fill that gap. “We tend to focus on the players that have left. For me, I’m focused on the players that are here, and they’re the ones I have to give the belief that they can come in and do the job for us. “We’re hoping that some of those boys will take the opportunity.” On building from the win in Thailand… “I was very happy with the way the trip went to Thailand. We know that when we play in Asia, the biggest challenge is travelling distances and conditions as well. “We went there, played against a very good side and put in a very good performance. We played really well and got the result. “But now we have to shift our focus to the A-League because it’s a completely different competition. Teams play in different ways, and I think we’re ready for it. “We want to use the confidence of winning that match and go into this match full of confidence and believing in what we do as a team.” On making a strong start… “It’s obviously important, but it’s a long season as well. “We just want to make sure that we do the things we want to do as a team, that we play the way we want to play and are able to execute the game plan that we put together for every match. “We want to focus on the processes, make sure that we understand what we need to do as a team, as a collective. “I believe if we do that, more often than not, you end up getting the results that you’re after.” Categories Club News Features Press Conference A-League Men Subscribe to our newsletter Keep up with our latest news and events. Op bezoek bij MVV Maastricht boekte de ploeg van Ruben den Uil een 0-3 overwinning. Yegoian was met twee doelpunten belangrijk voor de Kralingers, waarna Sliti in de slotfase de eindstand bepaalde. Yegoian opent de score Excelsior begon goed aan de wedstrijd in Maastricht en zocht vanaf de eerste minuten de aanval. Silva Timas zorgde met meerdere voorzetten voor dreiging, maar de thuisploeg wist het gevaar aanvankelijk weg te werken. Na een kwartier spelen was het alsnog raak voor de Kralingers. Van Gassel leverde opnieuw een assist af op Yegoian, die vanaf de linkerkant naar binnen trok en de bal via de binnenkant van de paal in de korte hoek schoot: 0-1. Drie minuten later kreeg Excelsior een uitgelezen mogelijkheid om de voorsprong te verdubbelen. Silva Timas veroverde de bal diep op de helft van MVV en kwam oog in oog met Wentges. De aanvaller probeerde de doelman te omzeilen, maar stuitte op de keeper en een verdediger. Na de sterke openingsfase van Excelsior kwam MVV beter in de wedstrijd. Daneels werd diep gestuurd en probeerde de uitkomende Van Gassel met een lob te verschalken, maar zijn inzet ging naast. Niet veel later probeerde hij het opnieuw, ditmaal van buiten het strafschopgebied. Zijn schot belandde recht in de handen van Van Gassel. De doelman wist met zijn vingertoppen een tweede treffer te voorkomen en tikte de bal over het doel. In het laatste kwartier voor rust bleef MVV de druk opvoeren. Sierra kreeg nog een mogelijkheid vanuit een lastige hoek, maar Van Gassel hield zijn korte hoek goed dicht. Aan de andere kant probeerde da Silva Moreira het van afstand en kopte Naujoks uit een voorzet van Yegoian, maar beide pogingen leverden geen doelpunt op. MVV kreeg via Liesdek een kopkans uit een hoekschop, maar zijn inzet ging naast. Even later ontstond er opnieuw gevaar voor het doel van Excelsior toen Dumont volledig vrij kwam te staan in het strafschopgebied. Dankzij goed verdedigend werk van da Silva Moreira kon Van Gassel op tijd ingrijpen. Excelsior schakelde direct om en bleef zoeken naar de tweede treffer. Die kwam er na een uur spelen. Excelsior 10 11 -3 Bekijk de hele ranglijst Excelsior heeft zondagmiddag op bezoek bij Fortuna Sittard een zure nederlaag geleden. De ploeg van Ruben den Uil kreeg meerdere mogelijkheden om de score te openen, maar wist het net niet te vinden. Diep in de blessuretijd ging het alsnog mis voor de Kralingers. Guth kopte in de 91e minuut de enige treffer van de wedstrijd binnen: 1-0. Kansen aan beide kanten De wedstrijd begon met een aantal aanvallende momenten voor Fortuna Sittard, maar Excelsior kwam al snel beter in het spel. De Kralingers zochten via combinaties over de flanken naar openingen in de verdediging van de thuisploeg. Na een kwartier spelen leverde dat de eerste doelpoging op. Yegoian speelde zichzelf goed vrij en legde de bal af op Groen, die vanuit een lastige hoek doelman Branderhorst op zijn weg vond. Ook Fortuna liet zich aanvallend zien. Halverwege de eerste helft moest Van Gassel meerdere keren in actie komen. De doelman hield zijn ploeg op de been met reddingen op twee schoten van Michut en plukte even later ook een afstandsschot van Van Ottele uit de lucht. Excelsior bleef ondertussen zoeken naar mogelijkheden, maar slaagde er ondanks enkele goed uitgespeelde aanvallen niet in om echt gevaarlijk te worden. Beide ploegen gingen daardoor met een 0-0 stand de rust in. Excelsior laat grote kans liggen Bij de start van de tweede helft kwam Thorsteinsson binnen de lijnen voor Naujoks waardoor Yegoian terug naar het middenveld ging. Excelsior begon sterk aan de tweede helft en kreeg al snel twee goede mogelijkheden. Eerst zag Sliti zijn schot nog net aangeraakt worden door Branderhorst, waarna een hoekschop volgde. Een minuut later kreeg Excelsior de grootste kans van de wedstrijd. Van Gassel zag Yegoian diep gaan en stuurde hem met een lange bal richting het doel van Fortuna. De verdediging van de thuisploeg zat mis, waardoor Yegoian alleen voor Branderhorst verscheen. Zijn inzet ging echter naast het doel. Ook Meissen kwam dicht bij de openingstreffer. Uit een hoekschop kopte de verdediger de bal hard voorlangs. Aan de andere kant was Fortuna gevaarlijk via Hübner, die zijn kopbal eveneens naast zag verdwijnen. Late domper in Sittard In de slotfase werd het spel steeds onrustiger en kreeg Fortuna meer mogelijkheden. Een kwartier voor tijd leek Romeny op weg naar de openingstreffer, nadat hij profiteerde van een verkeerde inspeelpass. Plug voorkwam met een uitstekende tackle dat de aanvaller alleen voor Van Gassel kon afronden. Excelsior probeerde met de ingevallen Jahanbakhsh en Janssen nog een overwinning uit het vuur te slepen, maar grote kansen bleven uit. Lange tijd leek het duel dan ook in een doelpuntloos gelijkspel te eindigen. In de blessuretijd ging het alsnog mis. Uit een hoekschop van Fortuna kon Guth van dichtbij raak koppen en de thuisploeg op een 1-0 voorsprong zetten. Daarmee kreeg Excelsior in de slotminuten een flinke domper te verwerken en bleef de ploeg met lege handen achter in Sittard. Doelpunten deze wedstrijd Excelsior Rotterdam 1. Stijn van Gassel (K) 3. IL MOMENTO DELLA SQUADRA «Quando si perde non si può essere certo di buon umore, la squadra si è resa conto che contro una Roma forte sarebbe però bastata un po’ più di attenzione per portare a casa un risultato. È qualcosa che ci farà crescere». LA LAZIO DI GATTUSO «La classifica parla chiaro. La Lazio è una squadra allenata da un grande uomo, oltre che da un grande allenatore. È in una condizione ottima, sia mentale che fisica. È la squadra che, insieme a noi, aveva performato di più. La differenza, secondo me, è tutta nell’energia: loro hanno continuato a mantenerla al netto dell’avversario e delle difficoltà che hanno avuto. Hanno una rosa profonda, talento e fisicità e, come tutte le squadre che stanno nelle zone alte della Serie A, sono stati allestiti bene». LE DIFFICOLTÀ E LE SCONFITTE «Quando si perde non fa piacere, indipendentemente da quello che metti dentro la gara. Bisogna che io dia una direzione alla squadra in questo momento, sono qui per questo. Abbiamo distribuito male le sconfitte nelle prime nove giornate e questo ci mette in guardia. L’energia, soprattutto nei momenti in cui bisogna fare trincea, è bassa. Prima c’era quasi un godimento individuale e collettivo nel cercare di non prendere gol. Adesso arriva un cross in area e magari sbagliamo le distanze e i riferimenti. È un aspetto su cui dobbiamo lavorare: se vogliamo fare punti e vincere, dobbiamo avere un’attenzione diversa». L’EQUILIBRIO DIFENSIVO «Le sconfitte consumano energia. Il nostro lavoro adesso è ricostruirla con chiarezza, responsabilità e la forza di aiutarci in campo. Credo molto nell’energia. Come ho sempre detto ai ragazzi, quando ci svegliamo la mattina c’è un uccellino che ci bussa alla testa, quello cattivo, e dobbiamo essere bravi a dominarlo. In questo momento sta facendo la differenza nella testa di ognuno di noi. Questa squadra nelle prime sei giornate è andata oltre le aspettative e io devo essere bravo a non far mancare la fiducia, a tenerli sul pezzo e ad alzare l’autostima. Tutto questo deve essere accompagnato da un’attenzione maniacale». LE SCELTE IN ATTACCO «Devo ancora valutare bene la condizione di tutti i giocatori, soprattutto di quelli che hanno giocato più di 60 minuti a Roma. Nzola ha fatto meglio quando aveva la palla e ha cercato di farsi trovare pronto quando non l’aveva. La nostra difesa parte dall’attacco e bisogna avere un atteggiamento ancora più propositivo nella prima pressione. Su Fadera valuteremo con lo staff e con l’area medica la sua condizione e può darsi che possa essere riproposto. Ci sarà qualche cambio, perché tre partite in una settimana, con la doppia trasferta, richiedono uno sforzo importante dal punto di vista fisico. Sono convinto che chi giocherà farà di tutto per invertire questo trend». IL CENTROCAMPO E IL RIENTRO DI WINKS «Deiola gioca bene sia lì in mezzo che dietro, perché mette sempre dentro le caratteristiche numero uno che voglio: l’atteggiamento, l’animo battagliero e lo spirito guerriero. Romano ha fatto una grandissima partita. Winks da ieri si allena con la squadra, valuterò se utilizzarlo. Così come per gli altri ragazzi, farò le scelte che riterrò più giuste. Abbiamo bisogno di Winks per fare le cose nelle nostre reali possibilità, anche quando abbiamo la palla. La squadra si è disimpegnata bene anche nel palleggio, ma in questo momento non ho una rosa profondissima per quanto riguarda i cambi in mezzo al campo. Le scelte dipendono esclusivamente dalla condizione dei singoli». IL RISPETTO DELLE AVVERSARIE «Nelle prime sei giornate questa squadra si è guadagnata il rispetto delle avversarie, ma questo non vuol dire che dobbiamo scioglierci alla prima difficoltà come neve al sole. Il problema non è quello che pensano gli altri, ma quello che noi possiamo inconsciamente pensare. Ci fa piacere quello che dice un avversario che in questo momento è in una forma ottima, ma deve anche alzarci le antenne. Ci aspetta una partita difficile contro una squadra che ha numeri importanti e vogliamo andare lì per cercare di fare una partita importante». LA CRESCITA DI SULEV «Ivan è un ragazzo che conosco benissimo, perché quando sono subentrato in Primavera era giovanissimo, forse aveva 15 anni. La società ha fatto un investimento importante portandolo in Italia, a Cagliari, dalla Bulgaria, credendo nelle sue qualità. Ha bisogno di tempo per inserirsi, ha la fortuna di avere un allenatore che lo vede da tre anni e mezzo, questo può aiutarlo nel percorso. Ha qualità tecniche chiare, ha piede e, dal punto di vista fisico, ha motore. È un ragazzo con qualità spiccate e io ci credo. Magari sarà domani, fra un mese o non sarà mai: dipende dagli eventi e da come si incastrano le cose. È comunque un giocatore che tengo in grandissima considerazione». SU SUGAWARA «Deve crescere in alcune richieste, ma questo non vuol dire che non sia in grado di fare la fase difensiva. Io voglio determinate cose in determinate zone del campo e il ragazzo si sta mettendo all’opera per esaudire queste richieste. È volenteroso, si fa voler bene da tutti. Penso che a Roma abbia fatto una buona partita dal punto di vista del palleggio. Quando si prende gol, soprattutto su un cross, sono coinvolti tre o quattro calciatori: magari le distanze e i riferimenti sono stati errati. Non me la sento di dare le colpe al ragazzo. È un professionista serio, un giocatore con qualità importanti e sono convinto che darà il suo contributo». L’ASSETTO TATTICO «La gara con la Roma è passata, l’abbiamo persa e siamo tornati con un pugno di mosche in mano. Ci sono stati spunti positivi e tante cose da analizzare e correggere, ma quella partita non fa più testo. Domani sarà una gara totalmente diversa, contro un avversario che gioca e attacca gli spazi in maniera differente. Dobbiamo capire cosa abbiamo fatto di buono e cosa abbiamo sbagliato a Roma, cercando di riproporre gli aspetti positivi e correggere quelli negativi. Contro la Roma abbiamo difeso a tre, a cinque e costruito a quattro, alzando Sugawara, con Fadera quasi da esterno alto e Nzola che faceva la boa. Domani potremmo vedere un assetto diverso, sia quando abbiamo la palla sia quando non l’abbiamo». IL RAPPORTO CON GATTUSO «Il complimento più bello che posso fare oggi a Gattuso è vederlo come un punto di riferimento umano, come uomo. Conosco Gennaro, lo stimo e conosco anche suo papà, quindi le sue radici. Sono contentissimo di quello che sta facendo, perché se lo merita. So quanto è stato male anche dopo la Nazionale. Dal punto di vista tecnico-tattico è un allenatore che ha più esperienza e più campionati di me. Prendo spunti da tutti e lui è uno di quelli che negli ultimi mesi ho voluto guardare, perché ho visto cose diverse rispetto a quello che faceva prima». SUI SINGOLI «Obert penso abbia pagato un po’ la Nazionale, dove ha giocato quasi tutte le partite. È arrivato a due giorni dalla gara con la Juventus e il ragazzo è encomiabile. Deve migliorare soprattutto nel prendere i riferimenti in area di rigore, cosa che nel secondo tempo contro la Roma ha fatto con Mancini. Ho fiducia in lui e deve stare tranquillo. Non penso sia scarico dal punto di vista fisico, anche se ha giocato tante partite e può pagare un po’ lo sforzo. Maldini me lo aspetto in campo. Ha un piccolo fastidio, un’infiammazione che si porta dietro da tempo, ma aveva bisogno di riposare. Quando è tornato dalla Nazionale si è allenato poco e ha sostenuto uno sforzo importante anche dal punto di vista emotivo. Questo mi ha permesso di farlo entrare a Roma e dargli un po’ di riposo. Se domani starà bene, sicuramente sarà della partita. Fazzini ha fatto un buonissimo lavoro in questo mese con l’area atletica. Siamo convinti che fisicamente sia cresciuto in modo esponenziale. È uno che domani potrebbe giocare dall’inizio. Trepy è stata forse una delle note più belle di Roma. Peccato perché, per l’azione che si era creato da solo, meritava un epilogo diverso. For one last time before playoffs, the New England Revolution will host Inter Miami CF at Gillette Stadium on Sunday night at 7:00 p.m. ET. The match marks the final test before Decision Day. WHERE TO WATCH Every Revolution match is available for streaming on Apple TV all season long. Watch: Apple TV Apple TV English Talent: Jake Zivin (Play-by-Play), Taylor Twellman (Analyst), Andrew Wiebe (Sideline) Apple TV Spanish Talent: Ammy Sadovnik (Play-by-Play), Diego Valeri (Analyst), Antonella Gonzalez (Sideline) Listen: 98.5 The Sports Hub HD2 (English); 1260 AM Nossa Radio USA (Portuguese); Rumba 97.7 FM English Radio Talent: Brad Feldman (Play-by-Play), Charlie Davies (Analyst) CURRENT FORM New England Revolution 2 nd in Eastern Conference (18-10-4, 58 pts.) Last Result | 3-2 win vs. Red Bull New York The New England Revolution are on a four-game win streak after taking down Red Bull New York 3-2 at Gillette Stadium on Wednesday night. The midweek victory kept the Revs at second in the Eastern Conference standings and secured homefield advantage for Round One of the playoffs. It was the 18 th victory for New England, setting a new second-best season record. The Revolution own the second-most home victories leaguewide and could match the home record of 12 wins with a three-point result on Sunday. New England are in strong form, winning seven of their last nine contests. Much of the Revolution’s success has come from their defensive resolve, with just 44 goals against, the Revs have conceded the third-fewest goals all season. Inter Miami CF 3 rd in Eastern Conference (15-6-11, 56 pts.) Last Result | 2-2 draw vs. FC Cincinnati Inter Miami enter Sunday’s match just two points behind the Revolution in the Eastern Conference standings. Powered by a league-leading attack that has scored 75 goals in 32 matches, the Herons have established themselves as one of MLS’s top sides. Miami hosted the Revs earlier this season in a tightly contested 1-1 draw. Despite their attacking firepower, Miami are winless in their last two outings after drawing FC Cincinnati midweek and falling to Red Bull New York last weekend. With the Revs looking to close their regular season home slate strong, it will be an exciting match between two of the East’s strongest sides. KEY PLAYERS Revolution goalkeeper Matt Turner Matt Turner made a combined 14 saves last week across the Revolution’s victorious two-game week. His 134 saves are the most of his career and the second-most among all goalkeepers this season. As the Revs face the league’s strongest attacking side, Turner’s shot-stopping abilities and leadership with be a key factor for New England. Turner owns six clean sheets this season and is on the verge of setting a new club single-season appearance record for a goalkeeper. With experience at the highest level, Turner’s poise becomes increasingly important as the Revs approach postseason action. Miami midfielder Lionel Messi Inter Miami’s attack begins with Lionel Messi. The Argentine star is on pace to claim his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot, leading the league with 25 goals while adding 15 assists for 40 goal contributions this season. Although Messi has been held scoreless in his last two appearances, his attacking threat remains undeniable. He leads MLS with 176 shots and 73 on target, making him the primary focus as the Revolution look to contain Miami’s potent attack. HEAR FROM THE REVS Head coach Marko Mitrović on Inter Miami CF’s potent attack and his assessment Sunday's opponent: “The last several years, they're very strong in the attack, not just this season. Overall, they have a lot of quality and experience around their team, and I think that with Miami, everybody knows who they are and what their strengths are as a team. We rely on ourselves, we rely on our team effort, and we know that we have to confront them as a team, knowing that we have one of the best teams in the league ahead of us with some amazing individuals. But it's another great opportunity for us to keep growing as a team. And again, those games can just help us to become a better team.” Matt Turner on his message to the fans ahead of Sunday’s regular season home finale: “Your support has been great all season. I think the Wednesday night was probably our lowest attendance of the entire season, which was a little disappointing given the form that we're currently in. But the reality is as we look forward to the future, we're going to need every single fan to come out and to support us. We're going to continue to put our best foot forward and hopefully continue to make you guys and all the fans proud of what we are as a team, the product we put out, our togetherness, and how we represent the region.” Turner on the impact of the team's mentality ahead of the postseason: “I think we've kind of taken every single game down this stretch as a playoff level atmosphere and playoff level intensity. Every single result really matters down the stretch, for jockeying for position, for keeping your playoff hopes alive, or whatever it is. So, the intensity, we've been up to the task for those really intense moments.” Emma Moneuse MLS Regular Season Copy URL Share on Facebook Share on X Related Stories Top four secured!
